the addition of controlled-release aspirin 75mg daily to heparin/warin in prior aspirin users with UA/NQMI at rest, was not superior to conventional aspirin in terms of clinical outcome.

the combination of controlled-release, prostacylin-sparing aspirin with anticoagulation is not superior to the combination of conventional aspirin with antcoagulation for the prevention of recurrent myocardial ischaemia in patients with unstable coronary syndromes already receiving aspirin.

aspirin users with UA/NQWMI at rest had similar rates of death, myocardial infarct, or stroke, whether they received a combination of aspirin plus antithrombotics or conventional aspirin plus anti-thrombotics.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

controlled-release aspirin plus antithrombotics, when added to standard antianginal therapy and compared with aspirin plus antitrombotics, was safe, well tolerated, and did not increase the risk of major ischemic events in prior aspirin users with rest unstable angina or rest non-Q wave myocardium infarction.

the combination of aspirin and anticoagulation was safe, and that the prostacyclin-sparingly formulated aspirin plus antithrombotics did not improve outcome in comparison to conventional aspirin plus the same antithromboties.
the prostacyclin-sparin formulation was not associated with a reduction in ischemic events or mortality, but was associated with a higher incidence of bleeding complications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a combination of antithrombotics, including aspirin, heparin, and warfarin, is effective and safe in the management of acute coronary syndromes.
aspirin-sparing therapy is safe and effective in the treatment of unstable angina and non-Q wave myocardia l infarction in patients already being treated with low-dose aspirin.
the use of a prostacylin-sparing aspirin formulation and anticoagulation in aspirin users is associated with improved outcomes compared with conventional aspirin and anticoagulatin.
